key_insight: Near-equilibrium agreement does not guarantee reliable fatigue dynamics: NequIP predicts roughly sevenfold lower intrinsic stacking fault energy than EAM and substantially more plastic deformation.
engineering_relevance: Fatigue simulations with foundational interatomic potentials need validation of driven, rare-event behavior beyond equilibrium benchmarks.
method: Compare EAM and foundational NequIP potentials on static and emergent properties.
Apply fatigue cycling to a nanoscale flaw modeled after the classical Griffith crack problem.
Analyze per-atom energy distributions after loading.
evidence_signal: Both potentials closely match reference data for many near-equilibrium properties, but their post-loading energy distributions differ most far above thermally accessible energies.
watch_item: Without direct experimental validation, potential-to-potential comparisons are informative but not definitive; memory-related crashes and silent extrapolation add practical risks.
paper_title: Emergent Fatigue Dynamics from Foundational Interatomic Potentials
